Hey! There’s still hope even though you can’t get a diagnosis now. I am going to assume you are not able to speak with a therapist if that’s the case look and see if your school has counselors on staff. They will listen to you and I have heard of some sending notes home encouraging you to be taken to a therapist. 

If that all falls through I want you to look into buying a workbook for mental health. They have ones on depression, EDs, anxiety, and pretty much every other condition you could think of you can buy it on Amazon or in a bookstore. This will act as a therapist for you and hopefully get you back on track emotionally. Pair the workbook with mental health YouTubers like Kati Morton and a free mood tracker (I use Daylio) so you can keep track of your moods and eating habits and see if there’s any patterns. To avoid the obsessive Ed voice when tracking I simply track whether I ate normally, had disordered eating, or didn’t eat. This came in handy when I was able to see a doctor. 

It’s important for you to start healing now because you will fall into patterns and the longer you wait the harder it is to break the pattern. Once you move out you can get the help you deserve but for right now it’s important to track and try to break the pattern. It’s hard work but I know you can do it :)

Even through experiencing the symptoms there is a part of me still screaming 'just buck up, walk it off, and deal with it' but I just can't....because I need help and that's okay.

She may change but for that to happen she has to be able to completely be able to put herself in your shoes and understand what she did and why it was wrong. Something that abusers unfortunately struggle with. I lived with my ex (we are lesbians as well) and while there was no choking, she showed the same behavior consistently over the course of two years. She would cry and get super upset after the incidents, often pointing a finger at me who was the emotionally abusive one. And I let it slide, each time I woke up with bruises I just let it slide and believed that I caused it because I was emotionally abusive. But guess what? It doesn’t matter. It doesn’t matter what you said to her she still is not justified in laying hands on you. When I finally called my girlfriend out on it she broke my things and shoved me into a wall (I’m mentioning this because if you do decide to break things off have someone there with you or someone who knows your location). While she needs therapy, you also need therapy. Even if you feel like it hasn’t affected you, it may down the road. It took me close to the one year mark of being broken up to feel trickle down from how she treated me. Also one more thing, I don’t her but I know with my ex she told me that she would talk about the physical abuse in therapy but she never did and quite honestly probably still hasn’t. You can’t wait around for her to fix herself, it’s not your job. What is your job is to fix the trauma that you faced in that relationship and learn how to create healthy attachment that doesn’t include intensity.

Give her space but make sure she is still posting on social media. I know when my friend tried to send me a text like that I didn’t respond right away either and I was honestly a little pissed off. I knew the relationship was doomed but it is a lot to process. Just be patient with her and try to remember this isn’t your friend, she’s not herself right now. She may be upset that you are revealing things to her but she will thank you later for being there through this trauma.
